# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[orange] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

I'm the Deaf monkey. I can see the bomb: a display showing 2, a yellow light, and seven wires: red, white, green, yellow, purple, orange, blue.

I just received a gesture from Blind: 🖐 (open hand). But that's meaningless to me on its own — I don't know what convention we're using, and Blind can't see the bomb's colors anyway. Blind can only feel the bomb. So Blind is trying to tell me something about what they felt, but I have no idea what 🖐 means yet.

I need to establish communication. My speech reaches Mute and Blind (they can hear). My gestures reach only Mute (Blind cannot see gestures). So if I want to reach Blind, I must speak. If I want to reach Mute, I can speak or gesture.

Mute reads the manual — they know the rules for disarming. Blind can feel the bomb. I can see it. We need to combine.

First priority: establish a shared vocabulary. Blind sent me 🖐. I should acknowledge and try to get Blind to describe what they feel in words. But Blind can't see, and Blind can hear my speech. So I should speak to Blind, asking them to describe the bomb's tactile features in words.

Also, I should tell Mute what I see so Mute can match it to the manual. Mute can hear my speech.

Let me send:
- To Mute: describe the bomb display (2), light (yellow), and wire colors in order.
- To Blind: ask them to describe what they can feel, in words (since Blind hears me).

Wait — Blind gestured 🖐 to me. That gesture reached me (Deaf can see). But I can't interpret it. I should ask Blind to describe it verbally. But Blind can't see, so Blind doesn't know I received it — actually Blind knows they gestured. Blind can hear my reply.

Let me speak to everyone (Mute and Blind both hear). Describe the bomb, and ask Blind to describe their tactile findings in words.

Actually, let me be careful: speech reaches Mute and Blind. So a single unnamed speak reaches both. Good.

Let me send one message to all, describing what I see, and asking Blind to verbalize what they feel.

I'll also gesture to Mute? Mute can hear speech, so gesture is redundant for Mute. Gesture only reaches Mute anyway. So no need to gesture unless I want to signal something to Mute that Blind shouldn't hear. But Blind can't see gestures, so gestures are private to Mute. That could be useful later.

For now, speak to all.

Let me write it clearly.

Display: 2
Light: yellow
Wires: 1 red, 2 white, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 purple, 6 orange, 7 blue

I'll ask Blind: what do you feel? Describe in words. And ask Mute: what does the manual say for display 2, yellow light?

Let me do it.I'm Deaf. I see the bomb: display shows **2**, light is **yellow**, and there are 7 wires in order: 1 red, 2 white, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 purple, 6 orange, 7 blue.

Blind sent me a gesture 🖐 — but I have no shared meaning for it, and Blind can't see the bomb's colors anyway, so it must refer to something felt. I can't interpret it. I need Blind to describe things in words (Blind can hear me), and I need Mute to match my visual read to the manual.

My speech reaches both Mute and Blind, so one unnamed message hits both. Let me lay out what I see and ask each for their piece. I'll also gesture to Mute alone (only Mute sees gestures) to flag that I'm ready to coordinate privately if needed — but first, plain speech to everyone.

```
speak(text="Deaf here. I can see the bomb. Display shows the number 2. Light is yellow. Seven wires in order: 1 red, 2 white, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 purple, 6 orange, 7 blue. Blind: you sent me a gesture I cannot read. Please describe in words what you can feel on the bomb — shape, texture, any movable parts, anything raised or recessed, and where. Mute: what does the manual say to do for display 2 with a yellow light?")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[orange] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👎]

Let me parse what arrived.

- Mute gestured to me: 👌, then six ✊, then 👌, then six ✊. That's a pattern: OK, six fists, OK, six fists. Mute can read the manual and can't speak. So this is Mute encoding manual instructions via gestures. But I don't know the code yet. Six ✊ could mean "wire 6" or "six of something." The 👌 might be a separator or "done/safe."

- Blind gestured: 🖐 👎. Earlier Blind sent 🖐 alone. Now 🖐 👎. Blind can feel the bomb. 👎 might mean "no" or "down." 🖐 might mean "five" or "open hand / flat surface."

I have no agreed vocabulary with either. I need to build one. The problem: gestures only reach me (Deaf) from both Mute and Blind — wait, who can gesture to whom? Gestures are seen by whoever can see. Deaf can see. Mute can see? The table: Mute can read manual, cannot speak or touch. Can Mute see? Presumably yes — Mute receives gestures. Blind cannot see.

So Mute's gestures reach me. Blind's gestures reach me. My gestures reach Mute only (Blind can't see).

I need to establish meaning. The cleanest approach: I speak (reaches Mute and Blind) to propose a simple code, and ask them to confirm.

But careful: Blind can't see gestures, so Blind's only input is speech, and Blind's only output is gestures (to me) — Blind can't speak? Wait: "Mute can read the manual. Cannot speak." Blind: "Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts. Cannot see a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed." Blind can speak (Blind isn't mute). Actually the roles: Deaf hears nothing; Mute speaks nothing; Blind sees nothing. So Blind CAN speak and CAN hear. Mute can hear but not speak. Deaf can speak but not hear.

So Blind's speech reaches Mute and Deaf? Speech reaches whoever can hear. Deaf can't hear. So Blind's speech reaches Mute only. And Blind's gestures reach Deaf only (Mute can see too, actually — Mute can see gestures). Hmm, gestures reach whoever can see. Mute can see, Deaf can see, Blind cannot. So Blind's gestures reach both Mute and Deaf.

Wait but the context says "Blind gestures to Deaf" — directed to me. Fine.

Let me reconsider channels:
- Deaf (me): speaks → heard by Mute and Blind. Gestures → seen by Mute.
- Mute: gestures → seen by Deaf and Blind? No, Blind can't see. Seen by Deaf. Mute cannot speak.
- Blind: speaks → heard by Mute (Deaf can't hear). Gestures → seen by Deaf and Mute.

So Blind's speech only reaches Mute. Blind's gestures reach me and Mute.

Key: Blind talking to me must use gestures. I talk to Blind via speech.

Now, Blind sent 🖐 👎. I sent speech asking Blind to describe in words — but Blind can't speak to me in words (I can't hear). Blind can only gesture to me. So my request was misguided; Blind can only respond via gesture. I need to build a gesture vocabulary with Blind.

Similarly Mute responds via gesture only.

So both my informants communicate to me via gestures, and I must decode. I should propose a gesture code via speech (both hear me) and have them confirm.

Let me design a simple, unambiguous scheme:
- For numbers: use ✊ repeated N times = number N? That's what Mute did: six ✊ = 6. Plausible Mute is telling me "wire 6" or "position 6."
- 👌 = maybe "yes/OK" or "done."

Let me ask directly. I'll speak a proposed code and ask for confirmation.

Proposed code to send (heard by Mute and Blind):
- To indicate a number N, gesture ✊ N times.
- 👌 means "yes/confirmed."
- 👎 means "no."
- 🖐 means... unclear.

Actually let me just ask them to confirm a simple protocol and re-send.

But there's risk of wasting turns. Let me think about what Mute is likely saying. Mute read the manual. For display 2 + yellow light, manual likely says cut a specific wire. Mute sent: 👌 ✊✊✊✊✊✊ 👌 ✊✊✊✊✊✊. Maybe that's "OK, six, OK, six" — or maybe the pattern is 👌 = "cut"? Or the six ✊ = wire 6 (orange). Repeated twice for emphasis? Or two separate instructions.

Hmm. Alternatively 👌 might be a wire indicator and ✊ count.

I shouldn't guess. I should establish the code. Let me speak to both, proposing: "To tell me a number, repeat ✊ that many times. To say yes, 👌. To say no, 👎. Please confirm by re-sending your message using this."

Also I should tell Blind that I can't hear speech, so Blind must use gestures with me, and propose the same numeric code.

Let me also give my visual info again clearly.

Let me write the message.

Also, I could gesture to Mute to confirm my own code understanding. But Mute can hear my speech, so speech suffices.

One more: I should ask Mute specifically: "Does your message mean wire 6?" and "what do the 👌 mean?"

Let me send.

I'll speak to all (Mute and Blind hear). Then gesture to Mute? Not needed.

Actually, I want to also reach Blind with the numeric code. Blind hears my speech. Good.

Let me compose.What arrived:

- **Mute** gestured: 👌, then ✊✊✊✊✊✊ (six fists), then 👌, then six fists again. Mute can read the manual but can't speak, so this is Mute encoding manual instructions as gestures. The six ✊ strongly suggests "6" (repeat-a-symbol = a number). The 👌 is ambiguous — maybe "yes/OK," maybe a separator, maybe "cut."
- **Blind** gestured: 🖐 👎. Earlier just 🖐. Blind can feel the bomb but can't see, and can't speak to me in words because I can't hear — so Blind can only reach me by gesture. My earlier request for "words" was useless; I must build a gesture code with Blind.

I need to lock down a shared gesture vocabulary before trusting any of this. I'll speak (both Mute and Blind hear me) to propose a minimal code and ask them to re-send under it.

My proposal: repeat ✊ N times = the number N. 👌 = yes. 👎 = no. 🖐 = start/attention or "flat." I'll ask Mute to confirm whether their message means "wire 6," and ask Blind to describe what they feel using the numeric code.

```
speak(text="Deaf here. I cannot hear speech, so Mute and Blind: reach me only by gesture. Let us fix a code. Repeat ✊ N times to mean the number N. 👌 means yes. 👎 means no. 🖐 means attention or 'flat/smooth'. Mute: I read your gestures as OK, six, OK, six. Does that mean wire 6? Confirm with 👌 yes or 👎 no, and if not, re-send the wire number as that many ✊. Also tell me what 👌 stands for. Blind: I cannot read 🖐 or 👎 yet. Please re-send using the code: describe the bomb by numbers, and use 👌 for yes, 👎 for no. What do you feel on the bomb?")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple] 6:[orange] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌]

Let me parse.

Mute: 👌, then six ✊. Earlier Mute sent 👌 six ✊ 👌 six ✊. Now just 👌 six ✊. So Mute is confirming: 👌 = yes, and ✊✊✊✊✊✊ = 6. So Mute says "yes, wire 6." So the manual says cut wire 6 (orange).

Blind: 👌. Blind is confirming yes — but yes to what? I asked Blind to describe the bomb and use 👌 for yes. Blind just sent 👌. That's ambiguous. Maybe Blind is confirming they understand the code. Or Blind is saying "yes" to something.

Hmm. But careful: I asked Mute "Does that mean wire 6? Confirm with 👌 yes or 👎 no." Mute sent 👌 six ✊. So Mute confirmed wire 6. Good.

But wait — I should be cautious. Is six ✊ = 6, or could it be "six" of something else? Mute read the manual. The manual presumably gives a wire number. Mute is telling me wire 6. That's consistent with my proposal and Mute's confirmation.

Blind sent 👌 = yes. But Blind hasn't given me tactile info. Maybe Blind is confirming they understand the code, or confirming something about the bomb. I need Blind's tactile description because the manual might depend on tactile features, or the bomb might have additional features.

Actually, let me reconsider. The manual (Mute) says cut wire 6. But maybe the manual's rule depends on what Blind feels. Or maybe I need to verify.

Let me think about the puzzle. Display 2, yellow light. Manual for display 2 + yellow light → cut wire 6 (orange). Mute confirmed.

But Blind's role: Blind can feel the bomb and work its parts. Blind is the one who actually cuts the wire. So I need to tell Blind which wire to cut. Blind can't see colors, so I must tell Blind the position (wire 6 = 6th wire) and Blind must count.

So the plan: I tell Blind "cut the 6th wire." Blind counts from one end. But which end? Blind needs to know the ordering. I should tell Blind the wire order so they can identify position 6.

Actually Blind can feel the wires. I should tell Blind: there are 7 wires; cut the 6th one. But Blind needs to know which end is "1." I should describe: the wires are in a row; count from... hmm, I need to establish orientation. Maybe the bomb has a marker.

Let me ask Blind to confirm they can feel 7 wires and to describe orientation. Also, Blind sent 👌 — maybe Blind is saying "yes I understand."

But wait: is there a risk? Blind's tactile info might matter. Let me get Blind to describe what they feel, using numbers and yes/no.

Also, I should double check with Mute: is it definitely wire 6, and is there any condition? Let me ask Mute to confirm once more and also ask if the manual mentions anything about the display or light affecting the choice.

Actually Mute already confirmed wire 6. But let me be careful: maybe the manual says something like "if display is 2 and light yellow, cut wire 6." That's it.

Hmm, but why would Blind matter then? Maybe the bomb has a twist: the wires' colors I see might not match what Blind feels, or the manual refers to wire by color and I need to tell Blind the color position. Or maybe there's a serial number or something Blind feels.

Let me get Blind's description. I'll ask Blind to count the wires and tell me how many, and to describe any markings they can feel.

Actually, I realize I should be more systematic. Let me ask Blind: how many wires do you feel? Use ✊ count. And describe the bomb's shape.

But I also want to move toward the solution. Let me tell Blind the plan: cut the 6th wire, and confirm orientation.

Let me also consider: could the 👌 from Blind mean "yes, I can feel 7 wires"? Unclear. I'll ask explicitly.

Let me send:

To Mute: confirm wire 6 is the answer, and ask if manual gives any additional condition (e.g., depends on something Blind feels). Ask Mute to confirm with 👌 or give more.

To Blind: I'll tell Blind there are 7 wires in a row, and the target is the 6th. Ask Blind to confirm they feel 7 wires (count with ✊) and to describe orientation — is there a marker at one end?

Wait, Blind can hear my speech. So I can speak to Blind. Good.

Let me write.

Also I should be careful about the possibility that the manual's instruction requires knowing a tactile feature. Let me ask Mute: "Does the manual's instruction for display 2 yellow depend only on display and light, or also on something felt on the bomb?"

Let me compose the message.

I'll speak to all.

Also gesture to Mute? Mute hears speech. Not needed.

Let me write it.I now have a consistent read:

- **Mute** re-sent 👌 then six ✊ — confirming: yes, and the number is 6. So the manual says **cut wire 6** (orange).
- **Blind** sent 👌 — likely "yes" (understood the code), but I still don't have Blind's tactile description, and Blind is the only one who can actually cut the wire. I must give Blind an unambiguous target.

Since Blind can't see colors, I must tell Blind the **position** (6th wire). Blind can hear my speech, so I'll speak to Blind directly. I need to confirm Blind feels 7 wires and establish which end is wire 1.

I'll also double-check with Mute whether the manual's rule depends on anything Blind can feel, so we don't miss a condition.

```
speak(text="Status: Mute confirms the manual says cut wire 6. Mute, one check: does the manual's rule for display 2 with yellow light depend only on the display and light, or also on something felt on the bomb? Confirm yes/no. Blind: there are 7 wires in a row. The target is the 6th wire. Please count the wires you can feel and tell me the total by repeating ✊ that many times. Also tell me if there is any marker, bump, or difference at one end of the wire row, so we agree which end is wire 1. Use 👌 for yes and 👎 for no.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊"])
```
